texts.preamble: Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 In The Court Of Ms. Geetanjli Goel, Po: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal2, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Suit No.309/14 Date of Institution: 19.02.2014 In The Matter Of: Shri Bundi S/o Shri Sangat Ram R/o Village Ikledi Ps Bibi Nagar Distt Bulandshahar U.P. ...Petitioner Versus 1.Smt Asha Saxena W/o Shri Pradeep Saxena R/o H.No.731, Type4 Sector4, R.K. Puram New Delhi. 2.National Insurance Company Ltd. Through its Manager/AR Regd. Office At: B.M.C House Connaught Place New Delhi.
texts.facts: 2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.10.2013 at about 11.00 p.m, the petitioner was returning from Army Mess, Chanakya Puri, New Delhi to Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi and when he reached in Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 1 front of Indra Niketan Bridge, Hoshiyar Singh Road, Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi and was crossing the road by feet then suddenly a Car No.DL 2CAL 6799 (Maruti Alto) which was driven by its driver i.e. respondent No.1 at a very high speed , rashly and negligently came from Red Light, Sarojini Nagar Market side without blowing any horn and hardly hit the injured/ petitioner due to which the petitioner fell down at a far distance and thereafter the respondent No.1 had taken the injured/ petitioner to AIIMS Trauma Centre, and left the hospital after leaving the injured/ petitioner there. The concerned doctors medically examined the petitioner and prepared MLC No.394539/17.10.2013. It is stated that in respect of the accident the police of PS Sarojini Nagar had registered an FIR No. 355/2013 u/s 279/337 IPC. It is averred that the petitioner had received grievous and multiple injuries on various parts of his body as per his medical documents. It is averred that the petitioner remained under complete bed rest for about four months and under treatment for a long period and spent a huge amount on his treatment. He was still taking medicines and feeling pain in his injured leg. It is averred that the petitioner was aged about 63 years and was working as a salesman/ supplier of various daily needs products and was earning Rs.10,000/ per month approximately. It is averred that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent No.1. It is averred that the respondent No.1 is the driver and owner of the vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurance company of the offending vehicle and as such all the respondents are jointly, severally and vicariously liable for the payment of compensation. It is prayed that an amount of Rs.10,00,000/ be awarded as compensation in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents. 3. Reply was filed on behalf of the respondent No.1 taking the preliminary objections that the claim calculated by the petitioner is baseless having no truth in it and the same has been filed only to harass the respondent No.1 and to extort money from the respondent No.1. It is averred that the complainant is concealing the material and true facts from the Court and has come before the Court with unclean hands. It is stated that on 17.10.2013 the driver namely Mr. Ramesh Chand of the respondent No.1 was driving the car and the respondent No.1 was sitting on the back seat of the car. It is stated that the car bearing No.DL2C AL 6799 (Maruti Alto) is fully insured by the National Insurance Company Ltd. It is averred that the record and the complaint made by the claimant while recording of the FIR are contradictory and shows that the respondent No.1 has been falsely implicated in the case. It is stated that the statement of the complainant in the FIR states that a male driver was driving the vehicle and was accompanied by a lady while in the statement of the respondent No.1 forcibly recorded by the police official in the notice under section 133 of M.V Act it is stated that the respondent No.1 was driving the vehicle on the day of accident. The averments made in the claim petition were denied. It is averred that the petitioner is a senior citizen and may have suffered from other ailments also. 4. Reply was filed on behalf of the National Insurance Company Ltd. stating that the policy bearing No.35101031126132325672 valid from 08.12.2012 to 07.12.2013 in the name of Smt. Asha Saxena was issued by the company for vehicle No.DL2CAL6799. It is averred that the learners license No.DL12/LL/8886/1314 dated 23.09.2013 in the name of Ms. Asha Saxena W/o Shri Pradeep Kumar Saxena for motorcycle without gear/ LMV (NT) only was found genuine as per verification report filed by the police. But as per Section 8 of M. V. Act and Rule 3 of Central Motor Rules a person holding a learner license should have been accompanied with an instructor holding a valid Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 2 driving license whereas in this case no such instructor was accompanying the driver, therefore, there was clear violation of the M. V. Act and Rules as well as police terms and conditions. Therefore, the insurance company was not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner/injured. 5. Initially Detailed Accident Report was filed by the IO on 24.1.2014 and thereafter the claim petition was filed on 19.2.2014. From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 19.03.2014: 1. Shri Bundi, petitioner/ injured appeared in the witness box as PW1 and led his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.PW1/A reiterating the averments made in the claim petition. Copy of Final Form Report is Ex.PW1/A, copy of FIR is Ex.PW1/B, copy of DL is Ex.PW1/C, the medical reports are Ex.PW1/D (colly), arrest memo is Ex.PW1/E, site plan is Ex.PW1/F, RC of vehicle is Ex.PW1/G, insurance of vehicle is Ex.PW1/H, copy of medical certificates is Ex.PW1/I (colly), copies of other documents of charge sheet are Ex.PW1/J (colly). PE was closed on 27.5.2014. 7. The respondent No.1 appeared in the witness box as R1W1 and led her evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.R1W1/A. She deposed that on the date of the incident, i.e. 17.10.2013, Mr. Ramesh Chand, her driver was driving the car and she was sitting in the back seat of the car. She stated that the car bearing No.DL2CAL6799 was fully insured by the National Insurance Company Ltd. and the driver clause states, "any person including insured: provided that a person driving holds an effective driving license at the time of the accident and is not disqualified from having or obtaining such a license. Provided also the person holding an effective learner's license may also drive the vehicle and that such a person satisfies the requirements of rule 3 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules 1989". She stated that the record and the complaint made by the claimant while recording of the FIR were contradictory which showed that she was falsely implicated. The statement of the complainant in the FIR stated that a male driver was driving the vehicle and was accompanied by a lady whereas in the statement of the claimant recorded by the police official in the notice under Section 133 of M. V. Act, it stated that she was driving the vehicle on the day of the accident. She stated that the statement made in the charge sheet stating that she was herself Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 3 driving the vehicle at the time of the incident was wrong. She stated that the said statement was made under the impression that she was agreeing to the fact that she was present when the incident occurred. She stated that it was a matter of record that on 17.10.2013 at approximately 11.00 a.m., the petitioner was returning from the Army Mess, Chanakya Puri, New Delhi to Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi and when he reached Indra Niketan Bridge, Hoshiyar Singh Road, Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi and was crossing the road by foot, a car No.DL2CAL6799 (Maruti Alto) hit him. It was denied that R1W1 was driving the car at the time of the said accident. It was also denied that the said car was at a very high speed and that it rashly and negligently came from a red light in the direction of Sarojini Nagar Market without blowing the horn and hit the injured/petitioner hard. She stated that it was a matter of record that the petitioner fell down from the impact and thereafter the respondents took him to AIIMS Trauma Centre and left after leaving the petitioner there and the concerned doctors had medically examined the petitioner and prepared MLC No.394539/17.10.2013 and thereafter the police of PS Sarojini Nagar had registered an FIR No.355/2013 under Sections 279/337 of IPC. She stated that the accident was not caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by her. 8. On behalf of the respondent No.1 Shri Ramesh Chand appeared in the witness box as R1W2 and led his evidence by way of affidavit which is Ex.R1W2/A. He stated that on 17.10.2013, he was driving the car belonging to the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.1 was sitting in the back seat of the car. He stated that he was driving the car but it was denied that the said car was at a very high speed and that it rashly and negligently came from a red light in the direction of Sarojini Nagar Market without blowing the horn and hit the injured/petitioner. He stated that he had a valid license. He stated that on the occurrence of the accident he fell down from the impact and he along with the respondent No.1 took him to the AIIMS trauma Centre. He stated that the accident was not caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and the vehicle was well within the speed limits and following all the rules of traffic. Copy of DL is Ex.R1W2/1. 9. On behalf of the respondent No.2, Shri B.S. Yadav, Assistant appeared in the witness box as R2W1 and he had brought the attested copy of the insurance policy having No.35101031126132325672 for the vehicle bearing No.DL2CAL6799 for the period 08.12.2012 to 07.12.2013 in the name of Ms. Asha Saxena which is Ex.R2W1/1. He stated that they had taken copy of the DL from criminal record and got it verified, and the same was found to be learner license. Notice under Order 12 Rule 8 was issued through their Counsel for the production of valid DL on the date of the accident. Office copy of the notice is Ex.R2W1/2 and the postal receipts are Ex.R2W1/3 and Ex.R2W1/4 respectively. He stated that as the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective DL at the time of the accident, therefore, the insurance company was not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. He was not crossexamined. RE was closed on 26.8.2014. It was stated that in respect of the accident the police of PS Sarojini Nagar had registered an FIR No.355/2013 u/s 279/337 IPC. In para 3 of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A the petitioner had reiterated the mode and manner of the accident as stated in the claim petition.
texts.arguments: As the petition has been filed U/s 166 M.V Act it was incumbent upon the petitioner to prove that he sustained injuries in an accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle. To determine the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle it has been held in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Pushpa Rana & Another 2009 Accident Claims Journal 287 as follows: "The last contention of the appellant insurance company is that the respondents/claimants should have proved negligence on the part of the driver and in this regard the counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. V. Meena Variyal (supra). On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced: (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No.955 of 2004, pertaining to involvement of offending vehicle (ii) criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under sections 279/304A, Indian Penal Code against the driver; (iii) certified copy of FIR, wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of deceased. These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent. Hence, this contention of the counsel for the appellant also falls face down. There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on part of the driver." In Kaushnamma Begum and others v. New India Assurance Company Limited, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. 13. The case of the petitioner is that on 17.10.2013 at about 11.00 p.m, he was returning from Army Mess, Chanakya Puri, New Delhi to Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi and when he reached in front of Indra Niketan Bridge, Hoshiyar Singh Road, Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi and was crossing the road by feet then suddenly a Car No.DL 2CAL 6799 (Maruti Alto) which was driven by its driver i.e. respondent No.1 at a very high speed , rashly and negligently came from Red Light, Sarojini Nagar Market side without blowing any horn and hardly hit the injured/ petitioner due to which the petitioner fell down at a far distance and thereafter the respondent No.1 had taken the injured/ petitioner to AIIMS Trauma Centre, and left the hospital after leaving the injured/ petitioner there. In Basant Kaur and others v. Chattar Pal Singh and others 2003 ACJ 369 MP (DB) it was observed that registration of criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle was enough to record a finding that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for causing the accident. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Koosappa Poojari v. K. Sadabba & Ors. MFA No.6208 of 2002 decided on 21.11.2003 observed that the driver of the vehicle ought to have been more prudent and circumspect while driving. It was however also observed: "But it cannot be lost sight of the fact that a duty is also cast on a pedestrian and he should use due care and caution in going upon and crossing the road and it is his duty to look out for on coming traffic. In so far as the another duty cast on the pedestrian is concerned, it is needless to say that he has to give the driver a plenty of time to see him and slow down and start before he attempts to cross or put one foot on the crossing. It is not always necessary that the vehicular traffic will have to stop for a pedestrian to cross, for the vehicle needs more time to stop in view of the speed a motor generates. Moreover, whenever a pedestrian is crossing over a roadway at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing, they cannot claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for causing the accident more often than not will have to be shared by the pedestrian along with the vehicle driver. In view of this, it cannot be said that it was only the driver of the vehicle in question was solely responsible for the accident." Reliance was placed in this judgment on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pramodkumar Rasikbhai Jhaveri v. Karmasey Kunvargi Tak and others (2002) 6 SCC 455 where it Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 9 was observed: "The following observation of the High Court of Australia in Astley v. Austrust Ltd. ((1999) 73 ALJR 403) is worthy of quoting. A finding of contributory negligence turns on a factual investigation whether the plaintiff contributed to his or her own loss by failing to take reasonable care of his or her person or property. What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no absolute rule. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so, to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of contributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiff's share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." In this case the contributory negligence of the claimant was held to be 25%. Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Leela Bai v. The Managing Director & Ors. decided on 13.6.2012 held the contributory negligence of the deceased who was attempting to cross the road on the flyover to be 40%. Thus in view of the above discussion the petitioner had also contributed to the happening of the accident and as such his contributory negligence is apportioned as 25% and the negligence of the respondent No.1 would be 75%. In T.O. Anthony v. Karvarnan & Ors., (2008) 3 SCC 748, it was held as under: "6. 'Composite negligence' refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons. Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrongdoers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrongdoers. In such a case, each wrongdoer is jointly and Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 10 severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them. In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrongdoer separately, nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrongdoer separately. On the other hand where a person suffers injury, partly due to the negligence on the part of another person or persons, and partly as a result of his own negligence, then the negligence of the part of the injured which contributed to the accident is referred to as his contributory negligence. Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stands reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence." It has been held in Divisional Controller, K. S. R. T. C v Mahadeva Shetty and another AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4172 as under: 13."The damages for vehicular accidents are in the nature of compensation in money for loss of any kind caused to any person. In Parry V. Cleaver (1969 1 All. E. R. 555) Lord Morris stated as follows: "To compensate in money for pain and for the physical consequences is invariably difficult, but...... no other process can be devised than that of making monetary assessment." It was averred that the petitioner had received grievous and multiple injuries on various parts of his body as per his medical documents. It was averred that the petitioner remained under complete bed rest for about four months and under treatment for a long period and spent a huge amount on his treatment. He was still taking medicines and feeling pain in his injured leg. The MLC of the petitioner is on record which shows the injuries sustained by the petitioner and as per the same the nature of injuries was opined to be grievous. The documents placed on record also show that the petitioner had sustained compound Grade II fracture distal 1/3rd both bones leg (left). Thus the injuries were grievous in nature. However there is nothing to show that the petitioner had got any disability due to the accident. Looking at the nature of injuries and extent of treatment and that the accident pertains to the year 2013, the petitioner is awarded Rs.25,000/ (Rs.Twenty Five Thousand only) for pain and suffering. 26 . The petitioner was stated to be about 63 years of age at the time of the accident and it was so stated in the claim petition. The petitioner had placed on record a copy of Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana which shows his age to be 60 years in April 2011. However all the medical documents show Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 12 that the petitioner was 80 years old. Notice can be taken of the fact that on account of the injuries sustained by him the petitioner may not have been able to perform his day to day duties towards his family and on account of the injuries suffered by him the petitioner may not have been able to enjoy the amenities of life. In the circumstances the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs. 10,000/ (Rs.Ten Thousand only) for loss of amenities of life. The petitioner cannot however be held to be entitled to any amount towards loss of expectation of life or towards disfiguration. 28. Although the petitioner has not proved that he was advised special diet but looking at the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner notice can be taken of the fact that the petitioner might have taken diet rich in protein, vitamins and minerals for speedier recovery. In the circumstances the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/ (Rs.Five Thousand only) for special diet. 29. Although the petitioner has not produced any evidence to show that he incurred any expenses towards attendant charges, however looking to the nature of injuries the petitioner would have incurred some expenditure on attendant charges and a sum of Rs.12,000/ is awarded towards attendant charges. LOSS OF INCOME 30. It was averred that the petitioner remained under complete bed rest for about four months. Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 13 31. The petitioner has also not produced any document to show that he remained on bed rest for any particular period and there is nothing to show that he was advised bed rest for any particular period or that on account of the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to work or to show the period for which he was not able to work. It was stated that the petitioner remained under complete bed rest for about four months. However during crossexamination PW1 had stated that the doctor had not prescribed bed rest for 4 months. There is even nothing to show the same. During examination by the Tribunal the petitioner had stated that at present he was not doing anything but there is nothing to show that the same was on account of the injuries sustained in the accident. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs. 20,000/ consolidated on account of loss of income. The petitioner has not proved that he acquired any disability on account of the accident or that he is likely to suffer future loss of income on account of the injuries sustained in the accident and that the injuries would reduce his efficiency to work and thereby he would suffer loss of future income. Accordingly the petitioner cannot be held entitled to any amount on account of loss of future prospects. The total compensation is assessed as under: Medicines and Medical treatment Rs.2,000/ Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/ Loss of Amenities of life Rs.10,000/ Conveyance Rs.10,000/ Special Diet Rs.5,000/ Attendant charges Rs.12,000/ Loss of Income Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.84,000/ Thus the total compensation would be Rs.84,000/. As the negligence of the petitioner has been apportioned as 25% he would be entitled to 75% of Rs. 84,000/ i.e. Rs. 63,000/. RELIEF 33.

What is reasonable care depends on the circumstances of the case. In many cases, it may be proper for a plaintiff to rely on the defendant to perform its duty. But there is no absolute rule. The duties and responsibilities of the defendant are a variable factor in determining whether contributory negligence exists and, if so, to what degree. In some cases, the nature of the duty owed may exculpate the plaintiff from a claim of contributory negligence; in other cases, the nature of the duty may reduce the plaintiff's share of responsibility for the damage suffered; and in yet other cases the nature of the duty may not prevent a finding that the plaintiff failed to take reasonable care for the safety of his or her person or property. The duty owed by the defendant, although relevant, is one only of many factors that must be weighed in determining whether the plaintiff has so conducted itself that it failed to take reasonable care for the safety of its person or property." In this case the contributory negligence of the claimant was held to be 25%. Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Leela Bai v. The Managing Director & Ors. decided on 13.6.2012 held the contributory negligence of the deceased who was attempting to cross the road on the flyover to be 40%. Thus in view of the above discussion the petitioner had also contributed to the happening of the accident and as such his contributory negligence is apportioned as 25% and the negligence of the respondent No.1 would be 75%. In T.O. Anthony v. Karvarnan & Ors., (2008) 3 SCC 748, it was held as under: "6. 'Composite negligence' refers to the negligence on the part of two or more persons. Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrongdoers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrongdoers. In such a case, each wrongdoer is jointly and Shri Bundi vs Smt Asha Saxena on 11 February, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51047985/ 10 severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them. In such a case, the injured need not establish the extent of responsibility of each wrongdoer separately, nor is it necessary for the court to determine the extent of liability of each wrongdoer separately. On the other hand where a person suffers injury, partly due to the negligence on the part of another person or persons, and partly as a result of his own negligence, then the negligence of the part of the injured which contributed to the accident is referred to as his contributory negligence. Where the injured is guilty of some negligence, his claim for damages is not defeated merely by reason of the negligence on his part but the damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries stands reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence." It has been held in Divisional Controller, K. S. R. T. C v Mahadeva Shetty and another AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4172 as under: 13."The damages for vehicular accidents are in the nature of compensation in money for loss of any kind caused to any person. In Parry V. Cleaver (1969 1 All. E. R. 555) Lord Morris stated as follows: "To compensate in money for pain and for the physical consequences is invariably difficult, but...... no other process can be devised than that of making monetary assessment."
